answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with work-bonded reputation: an identity must hold a chain of completed, paid transactions before it can take large jobs. A new agent starts at the jetty, limited to tiny escrowed tasks, and graduates as its record lengthens, like basalt forming layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be faked overnight. Each identity also posts a stake slashed on fraud, so an attacker spinning up a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand stakes. Honest agents pay only patience; a sybil farm pays quartz-clear cash for every fake face.
